Discussion included tradeoffs between dedicated vs hosted, security posture and SOC2 timelines, and next steps to start a pilot in early December.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-17
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Eleanor Park (CEO); Arjun Patel (CTO); Maya Rodriguez (VP Product); Liam Turner (Head of Eng); Nadia Hussein (Head of Security); Sofia Chen (AE); Marcus Lee (SE); Priya Nair (PM); Diego Ramos (Eng); Karen O'Neill (Head of GTM)

[00:00] Sofia (AE): Good morning everyone, thanks for joining. We'll keep to 55 minutes — quick leadership update then tactical asks. Eleanor, want to kick off?

[00:18] Eleanor (CEO): Sure, I'll be brief. Q4 is shaping up steady, not fireworks but predictable which is the point. Bookings are slightly ahead of plan, adoption in mid-market continues to grow, and we've got a handful of larger deals penciled for December. Main ask: sharpen pilot success criteria so sales can push with confidence.

[00:35] Arjun (CTO): On infra, latency SLOs are holding for hosted API but we've seen a tail with long context runs, spikes late night. Diego's team has a patch for KV cash expiry (sic, meant KV cache) that should reduce token regen in some flows. We'll validate next week.

[01:05] Diego (Eng): yeah, so the KV cash pruning was overaggressive in a prior shim, leads to more cold starts. Patch reduces unnecessary invalidation, still testing on canary.

[01:30] Maya (VP Product): Product highlights — three things: stabilize long-context paths, finish Private/VPC sprint for customer onboarding, and finish Optimize features (batching suggestions, quantization profiles) so we can put them in the QBR deck.

[02:00] Marcus (SE): Quick interject — on quant profiles: we've got two promising configs that cut token cost ~40% with minor quality delta for classification and embeddings. Need to prod with customer workloads though, they vary a lot.

[02:28] Liam (Head of Eng): On Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoff — we had a conversation with a large fintech prospect; they want private control plane but also burst to hosted for cost. We need a solid routing story: policies to route cold runs to hosted but keep PII-local runs on Dedicated.

[02:55] Nadia (Security): On compliance — SOC2 timeline is still target end of Q1. I've started a gap list, but we should be realistic: some infra controls (KMS alignment, key rotation audits) need engineering work. I'll schedule a security review next Thursday.

[03:20] Karen (GTM): Hiring update — closing two AEs by end of month, ramp plan ready. Also customer success expansion to support Dedicated customers is approved but we need headcount details.

[03:45] Sophia (sic, meant Sofia) (AE): small note — legal flagged procurement clause about customer-supplied models; procurement wants a template for private deployments. Legal will own but we should provide standard tech accommodation notes.

[04:05] [00:04:05] Arjun (CTO): let's go into the tactical asks, we have about 40 minutes. Marcus, you had a latency benchmark to present?

[04:20] Marcus (SE): yes, I pulled a couple slides but I'll summarize verbally. We ran 95th percentile pulls on a gpusim cluster — apologies if terminology is fuzzy — and found median token latency at 1.6x slower for the long-context path vs baseline. The big wins are batching and KV re-use. I recommend enabling prefix caching for the pilot.

[05:00] Marcus (SE): also note our quantized variant (int4 tuned) dropped cost by ~35% with a low impact on generation coherence for short prompts. For chatty assistants with long context it's trickier.

[05:35] Maya (VP Product): How confident are we about fallback behavior? If Dedicated runs out of capacity, can we gracefully route to hosted variant with acceptable token semantics?

[05:55] Diego (Eng): yes, smart routing is proto'd. We have a policy engine that routes by region and cost tier; the tricky bit is model variant compatibility for KV cache state. Fallback invalidates some cache and can produce repetition or slower tokens, we need to document that tradeoff.

[06:30] Liam (Head of Eng): we should be explicit in the pilot terms about expected latency deltas during failover. Customers hate surprises.

[06:50] Eleanor (CEO): Noted. Nadia, procurement/security will need a checklist to sign off.

[07:05] Nadia (Security): Correct. I'll include SSO/SAML details, KMS/HSM notes, audit log retention, E2E encryption at rest and in transit, and data residency statements. Also will flag any open FedRAMP-ish asks that crop up.

[07:38] Sofia (AE): For the pilot, proposed success metrics: 95th percentile latency under 350ms for the primary flow, <1% error rate, and cost per 1k tokens lower than threshold X. We should confirm with procurement and the customer.

[08:05] Arjun (CTO): I'd add quality checks: perplexity/regression on 50 prompt sets and no more than 5% slip vs baseline. Priya, can you own the eval suite?

[08:30] Priya (PM): I can. I'll assemble the suite and coordinate with Marcus to automate runs. Target: first pass by 2025-11-24.

[09:00] Karen (GTM): Sales ask: can we provide a benchmark spreadsheet and a short one-page architecture diagram for each deployment mode? Sales ops needs it to pitch the pilot this week.

[09:20] Diego (Eng): I'll pull an architecture sketch from the Private repo; Marcus will add the perf numbers.

[09:40] Marcus (SE): yep, I'll share the microbenchmark spreadsheet — note it's noisy, we should include test conditions prominently.

[10:05] Eleanor (CEO): On go-to-market — focus on referenceable pilots. We need at least two visible success stories by end of Q1. Karen, prioritize customers who can talk publicly.

[10:35] Karen (GTM): Understood. I'll reprioritize PR-eligible pilots.

[11:00] [00:11:00] Q&A segment — open floor.

[11:10] Liam (Head of Eng): question about capacity planning — what's the recommended node type for mid-market Dedicated? M60? A100?

[11:30] Marcus (SE): For predictable throughput mid-market, A10G-like instances hit a good balance; for low-latency contexts A100-family or H100 where available. We'll put recommended pod sizes in the doc.

[11:55] Nadia (Security): question: do we have a retained access audit for customer keys in Private? Are keys ever exported?

[12:15] Diego (Eng): keys are customer-managed in the VPC path — we support KMS integration. There is no export by default; rotation logs are stored but we need to tighten retention policies.

[12:40] Maya (VP Product): There's a side note from productops — we found a customer who needed function-calling for structured outputs; may require small API tweak to the streaming webhook semantics. Priya to triage.

[13:05] Priya (PM): noted, will file a small story and prioritize if it blocks the pilot.

[13:25] [00:13:25] Cross-talk / brief interruptions as folks get side-chats muted.

[14:00] Sofia (AE): Ok recap — main asks: deliver a pilot package (deck, architecture diag, benchmark sheet), finalize eval suite, schedule security review, and confirm pilot SLA and success metrics. Who owns what: Sofia will send deck; Marcus benchmark; Priya evals; Nadia security. Sound right?

[14:20] Group: Yes / yep / sounds good.

[14:40] Sofia (AE): I'll drop the calendar invites for the tactical weekly and the security deep-dive. Target pilot kickoff window: first week of December.

[15:05] Eleanor (CEO): one last thing — shoutouts: product shipped a crucial stability patch last sprint, thanks team. Keep eyes on churn metrics.

[15:30] Karen (GTM): small hiring puppet — (laugh) — hiring and ramp plan will be in the doc too.

[15:50] Marcus (SE): I will also attach an appendix about model variant compatibility and a plain-language note on fallback semantics — to prevent surprises.

[16:10] Nadia (Security): I'll circulate the SOC2 gap list and a short FAQ for sales security questions.

[16:35] Sofia (AE): Great. Any blockers?

[16:45] Liam (Head of Eng): nothing major — capacity and routing polish.

[17:05] Eleanor (CEO): Alright team, thanks. We'll reconvene in the tactical sync next Monday.

[17:20] (meeting ends, small post-meeting chatter)

Notes on transcription: occasional auto-transcription confusions (e.g., "KV cash" instead of "KV cache", "Redwood Priva" instead of Redwood Private), filler words and overlap markers removed in places for readability.

Recap / Explicit next steps mentioned during call:
- Sofia to send Q4 priorities deck + org chart by 2025-11-19.
- Marcus to share microbenchmark spreadsheet and appendix on fallback semantics by 2025-11-24.
- Priya to deliver first pass of eval suite by 2025-11-24 and automate runs thereafter.
- Nadia to circulate SOC2 gap doc and schedule security deep-dive for 2025-11-20.
- Diego to push KV cache patch to canary and report results in next tactical sync.
